er_v06_c19_b102_10: Tomorrow I'll come by even if I'm not buying anything.
er_v06_c19_b102_12: She stands, lets go of your hand, and steps back half a pace to clear the shutter.
er_v06_c19_b103_01: I see you as a friend. That won't change.
er_v06_c19_b103_02: ...Good to be clear. Saves me guessing.
er_v06_c19_b103_03: I'll sell as usual tomorrow. Fair price—not a single credit off.
er_v06_c19_b103_04: She stands, pushes the crate outside the window back into place, and walks off under the streetlights.
er_v06_c21_b001_01: Today I really am here to shop.
er_v06_c21_b001_02: Last time I made a decision for Eleanor and angered her—I went and apologized.
er_v06_c21_b001_03: She snapped that I shouldn't only apologize to the shopkeeper, as if she has no mouth of her own.
er_v06_c21_b001_04: I saw her mother too. She's thinner, but her temper hasn't changed—still won't stand for idle praise.
er_v06_c21_b002_01: By the way, I had that bracelet appraised by an expert. Your offer was fair.
er_v06_c21_b002_02: I told people on the Upper Level, and they didn't believe the Lower Level had a shopkeeper like you.
er_v06_c21_b003_01: When I used to choose gifts, I only worried they weren't expensive enough.
er_v06_c21_b003_02: Now Eleanor tells me to bring things that are actually useful, not turn a visit into an exhibition.
er_v06_c21_b003_03: She has a point, but her tone makes it hard to admit it right away.
er_v06_c21_b004_01: Eleanor told me flat out you're together, with no intention of asking my opinion.
er_v06_c21_b004_02: Now word on the Upper Level is that she's fallen for a Lower Level pawnshop owner.
er_v06_c21_b004_03: I deflected a few remarks for her along the way.
er_v06_c21_b004_04: Those people were targeting Eleanor. I couldn't let them spread rumors.
er_v06_c21_b005_01: Eleanor told me you're a friend worth keeping.
er_v06_c21_b005_02: She hardly ever uses the word 'worth.' If I praise her to her face, she just says I talk too much.
er_v06_c21_b006_01: If a good business opportunity comes up later, I'll send someone straight to you.
er_v06_c21_b006_02: If the goods are right and the price is right, we'll talk.
er_v06_c21_b006_03: Pfft. No wonder that's all Eleanor says now.
er_v06_ep_b001_01: Why haven't you fixed that broken lamp of yours yet?
er_v06_ep_b001_02: My chipped cup still holds water fine—but you just stood there and watched me pick a chipped one.
er_v06_ep_b002_01: Here. My mom made an extra portion and had me bring it over.
er_v06_ep_b002_02: ...Don't ask her how she always happens to make exactly one extra.
er_v06_ep_b002_03: Eat it while it's hot. If it goes cold, I'm not reheating it for you.
er_v06_ep_b003_01: I used to know the one who just left. Always telling me to keep away from Lower Level people.
er_v06_ep_b003_02: So I told him: buy your goods and mind your manners. Want to lecture me about boyfriends? Then leave.
er_v06_ep_b003_03: And he actually bought his things and left, all well-behaved.
er_v06_ep_b004_01: I just got paid today. Don't even think about waiving my bill.
er_v06_ep_b004_02: I'm not just someone for you to look after. I can look after people too.
er_v06_ep_b004_03: Settle the bill first, then keep me company a while.
er_v06_ep_b005_01: I sorted the goods by quality, and picked out the broken parts separately.
er_v06_ep_b005_02: I'm at least half a veteran now. No more bringing up my first scavenging trip.
er_v06_ep_b005_03: All right, let's see what today's haul is worth.
